content:
The Profit, Loss & Discount chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Profit, Loss & Discount tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Profit, Loss & Discount

Cost price, selling price, markup and marked price, single and successive discounts, and dishonest-dealer / false-weight problems.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Profit% and Loss% are always taken on the cost price.
  • SP = CP·(100+Profit%)/100; CP = SP·100/(100+Profit%).
  • Two successive discounts a%, b% ≡ single discount a + b − ab/100 %.
  • Selling two items at the same price, one at +x% and one at −x%, gives a net loss of (x/10)²%.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Taking profit% on the selling price instead of cost price.
  • Adding two discounts directly instead of using the successive formula.
  • Forgetting the guaranteed loss in the equal-SP +x%/−x% trap.

faq.q: Do profit and loss percentages use CP or SP?
faq.a: Always the cost price, unless the question explicitly says otherwise.
Apply them one after another, or use the shortcut a + b − ab/100. Two 10% discounts give 19%, not 20%.
